blind_spots.blind_spot: No accreditation path for the 'secure, online dashboard' their DoD offering depends on
blind_spots.operator_reality: An ADRS alert feed consumed by USSPACECOM/SDA operators must live on accredited government networks — RMF package, IL4/IL5 hosting, STIGs, a sponsor for the ATO. A commercial web dashboard demo cannot be plugged into a Space Force ops floor, and the ATO clock (12-18 months) can outrun their Phase II period of performance.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founding team is aerospace radiation scientists and entrepreneurs; nothing in 1,477 words of own language touches ATO, RMF, IL levels, CMMC, or ITAR despite marketing directly to DoD space customers.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Secure, online dashboard to track mission radiation risk analytics, trends and alerts (pre-mission, on-station, post-mission)

blind_spots.blind_spot: TRL 3/4 core system with the Phase II clock already running since 2023
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their own abstract says the goal is to 'demonstrate the feasibility' of ADRS at TRL 3/4 — feasibility, not fielding. When the D2P2 period of performance ends, the gap from TRL 4 demo to an operational SDA tool (integration with Space Force C2 systems, government back-end data feeds, sustainment) is exactly the months-to-field > funded-months trap; for a ~4-person company one dead transition is the company.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The abstract measures success in MTTR benchmarks versus current practice — a lab metric — with no named transition sponsor, program office, or Phase III pathway.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Atlantis aims to perform R/R&D to demonstrate the feasibility of our Anomaly Detection and Response System (ADRS) technology (TRL 3/4)

blind_spots.blind_spot: Countermeasure recommendations with no advocacy chain into satellite operations centers
blind_spots.operator_reality: ADRS 'generate[s] recommended evasive countermeasures or maneuvers' — but a maneuver recommendation from an outside vendor tool only matters if an ops-floor crew commander is authorized to act on it. That requires integration into existing space C2 workflows and a champion above the analyst level; analysts liking the dashboard is not adoption.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: All own-language is capability-first (sensors, models, AI) aimed at 'commercial, civil and DoD satellites' generically; no named operational unit, CONOPS, or ops-workflow integration appears anywhere.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: generate probabilistic SEE models and countermeasures for protecting on-orbit assets

opener_hook: Atlantis's 2023 D2P2 abstract targets feasibility of ADRS at TRL 3/4 against USSPACECOM's SDA gap — the distance from that demo to an accredited ops-floor tool is where the funded months usually run out.
what_they_do: Space-radiation modeling, sensors, and AI anomaly-detection (ADRS) to protect satellites and crews from space-weather effects.
